references.text: The warning against following other gods and the punishment for idolatry. Those who entice others to worship other gods shall be put to death.
The law prescribing the death penalty for anyone who worships other gods or heavenly bodies, which is an abomination to the Lord.
The Israelites worshipped Baal-Peor and sacrificed to foreign gods, provoking the Lord's anger and judgment.
The command to fear the Lord alone and serve only Him, not following other gods.
The first and second commandments: You shall have no other gods before Me, and you shall not make for yourself an idol.
Israel sacrificed to demons that were not God, to gods they had never known.
Elijah's challenge to the people to choose between the Lord and Baal—you cannot limp along on both sides.
Paul warns against sacrificing to idols and having fellowship with demons, for one cannot partake of both the Lord's table and the table of idols.
Leviticus 27:28 defines the term 'ban' (herem) used in Exodus 22:19 to describe the fate of those who sacrifice to other gods.
Psalm 97:7 confirms the consequence of the violation in Exodus 22:19 by showing that idolaters will be put to shame while the Lord is exalted.
1 Corinthians 10:20 reveals the spiritual reality behind Exodus 22:19 by showing that sacrifices to other gods are actually sacrifices to demons.
